title: What smart people are saying about OpenAI's 'Apple is getting this wrong' rebuttal
excerpt: In a blog post, OpenAI wrote that Apple's recent lawsuit was "careless, aggressive and oddly personal." Here's what smart people are saying about it.
content_html:
By Ben Shimkus

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

OpenAI is clapping back against Apple's lawsuit.

On Monday, the AI company published a blog post titled "Apple is getting this wrong," accusing the iPhone maker of presenting a misleading account of the events behind its trade-secret lawsuit. OpenAI highlighted what it said were errors in Apple's legal correspondence and released messages that it said provided important context about the dispute.

"Apple is one of the greatest companies of all time, and built a reputation for obsessing over the smallest details," the post says. "This careless, aggressive and oddly personal lawsuit sadly doesn't live up to that reputation."

Apple sued OpenAI in July, alleging that the ChatGPT maker benefited from trade secrets taken by former Apple employees. The lawsuit alleges, among other things, that Chang Liu, a veteran Apple engineer, improperly retained and accessed confidential company information after leaving for the AI lab in January.

OpenAI — which is trying to develop its own hardware products — previously denied wrongdoing, saying it is not interested in Apple's secrets.

Monday's post takes the AI lab's defense a step further. It said that Apple employees reached out to Liu after he left for OpenAI in January and said Apple is "failing to properly manage system access when people leave."

Here is what smart people are saying about the post:

Elon Musk, CEO of Tesla and SpaceX

Apple is seeking expedited discovery and a preliminary injunction, per Monday court filings. That suggests that the company believes other former employees may have retained or accessed confidential information after joining OpenAI.

Elon Musk, the outspoken Tesla and SpaceX CEO who lost a lawsuit against OpenAI and its leaders earlier this year, reposted screenshots of Apple's latest court filings on Tuesday.

"Can't trust OpenAI," he wrote.

Neil Cybart, Founder of Above Avalon

Neil Cybart, the founder of the independent Apple analysis firm Above Avalon, dismissed OpenAI's response in a post on X.

He described the post as "nonsensical" and accused OpenAI of using the classic "hey, look over there" strategy to draw attention away from Apple's central allegations.

"OpenAI must be really nervous about Apple's trade secret theft lawsuit because this silly attempt at PR spin is nonsensical," Cybart wrote.

Jim Cramer, host of CNBC's "Mad Money"

Jim Cramer, CNBC's host of "Mad Money," also commented on Apple's preliminary injunction in a post on X.

"Gloves off," he wrote.

Todd Dailey, former Apple enterprise marketing manager

Todd Dailey, a former Apple enterprise marketing manager who spent 22 years at the company according to his LinkedIn, said his own departure made OpenAI's statements about Apple's offboarding problems seem plausible.

On X, he wrote that he still had two unreleased Apple prototypes.

"Old Apple wouldn't have let an ex-employee hold a prototype for more than 24 hours and would have sent someone to my door to get it," Dailey wrote.

He said the experience reflected how stretched Apple's employees had become and made it easier to understand how the company's lawyers could have made mistakes in their correspondence with OpenAI.

"I'm not surprised at all that busy, harried lawyers could make this mistake," he wrote.

Harpal Singh, founder of Blimpp

Harpal Singh, the founder of the generative-engine-optimization platform Blimpp, told Business Insider that OpenAI's post was written to directly contradict Apple's account.

That tactic, he said, could affect how journalists, search engines, and AI tools describe the lawsuit.

"OpenAI is not just defending itself in court," Singh said. "It wants to present the narrative that journalists, search engines, and other AI Response Systems will mirror."

周一，这家人工智能公司发表了一篇题为“苹果公司犯了错误”的博文，指责这家 iPhone 制造商对其商业秘密诉讼背后的事件提供了误导性的描述。 OpenAI 强调了苹果法律信函中的错误，并发布了一些消息，称这些消息提供了有关争议的重要背景。

帖子中写道：“苹果是有史以来最伟大的公司之一，并以注重细节而闻名。” “遗憾的是，这场粗心、咄咄逼人和奇怪的个人诉讼并不符合这一声誉。”

苹果于 7 月起诉 OpenAI，指控 ChatGPT 制造商从苹果前员工窃取的商业机密中受益。 该诉讼称，苹果资深工程师刘畅在一月份离开人工智能实验室后，不当保留和访问了公司机密信息。

试图开发自己的硬件产品的 OpenAI 此前否认有不当行为，称对苹果的秘密不感兴趣。

周一的帖子使人工智能实验室的辩护更进一步。 据称，在刘一月份离职前往 OpenAI 后，苹果员工联系了刘，并表示苹果“未能在人们离开时妥善管理系统访问”。

以下是聪明人对这篇文章的评价：

埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk)，特斯拉和 SpaceX 首席执行官

根据周一向法庭提交的文件，苹果正在寻求快速证据发现和初步禁令。 这表明该公司认为其他前员工在加入 OpenAI 后可能保留或访问了机密信息。

直言不讳的特斯拉和 SpaceX 首席执行官埃隆·马斯克（Elon Musk）今年早些时候在针对 OpenAI 及其领导者的诉讼中败诉，他周二转发了苹果最新法庭文件的屏幕截图。

“不能相信 OpenAI，”他写道。

尼尔·赛巴特 (Neil Cybart)，Above Avalon 创始人

苹果独立分析公司Above Avalon 的创始人Neil Cybart 在X 上的一篇帖子中驳斥了OpenAI 的回应。

他称该帖子“毫无意义”，并指责 OpenAI 使用经典的“嘿，看那边”策略来转移人们对苹果核心指控的注意力。

Cybart 写道：“OpenAI 一定对苹果公司的商业秘密盗窃诉讼感到非常紧张，因为这种愚蠢的公关尝试是荒谬的。”

吉姆·克莱默 (Jim Cramer)，CNBC 节目“Mad Money”的主持人

CNBC 节目“Mad Money”的主持人吉姆·克莱默 (Jim Cramer) 也在 X 上的一篇帖子中对苹果的初步禁令发表了评论。

“脱掉手套，”他写道。

托德·戴利（Todd Dailey），前苹果企业营销经理

前苹果企业营销经理托德·戴利 (Todd Dailey) 在该公司工作了 22 年，LinkedIn 称，他自己的离职使得 OpenAI 关于苹果离职问题的说法似乎有道理。

在 X 上，他写道，他还有两部未发布的苹果原型机。

戴利写道：“老苹果不会让前员工持有原型超过 24 小时，并且会派人到我家门口取。”

他表示，这次经历反映了苹果员工的压力有多大，也让人们更容易理解该公司的律师在与 OpenAI 的通信中为何会犯错误。

他写道：“忙碌的律师可能会犯这样的错误，我对此并不感到惊讶。”

哈帕尔·辛格（Harpal Singh），Blimpp 创始人

生成引擎优化平台 Blimpp 的创始人 Harpal Singh 告诉 Business Insider，OpenAI 的帖子是为了直接与苹果的说法相矛盾。

他说，这种策略可能会影响记者、搜索引擎和人工智能工具如何描述这起诉讼。

“OpenAI 不仅仅是在法庭上为自己辩护，”辛格说。 “它希望呈现记者、搜索引擎和其他人工智能响应系统将反映的叙述。”
